$comment: KRYLO's Codex hook set (docs/adr/0029-codex-host-packaging-and-approval-boundary.md). Unlike Claude (ADR-0021, hooks scoped to the run Skill's own frontmatter), Codex plugin-bundled hooks have no Skill-scoped lifecycle and fire for every ordinary Codex session -- every entrypoint below implements the inactive-run no-op path (resolve identity, check for an active KRYLO run, exit 0 with no output and no state mutation if none) so a session that never invokes $krylo-run pays only the measured no-op latency budget. Referenced explicitly via .codex-plugin/plugin.json's own "hooks" field, not auto-discovered, so this never collides with Claude's separate (deliberately empty) hooks/hooks.json. Matcher includes "Bash" first: a real installed codex-cli 0.120.0 binary's own embedded PreToolUse JSON schema constrains tool_name to the literal const "Bash" for every command hook invocation (independently confirmed by direct byte inspection of codex.exe, not merely documentation) -- the other alternatives are kept as forward-compatible matches for a future/different build that differentiates further, per current published docs, but must never be relied on alone. PermissionRequest is deliberately NOT registered here: "PermissionRequest" is absent from this build's own embedded HookEventNameWire enum (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop only) -- registering an event this build does not recognize risks the whole file failing to parse and silently dropping PreToolUse/PostToolUse with it, an unacceptably fail-open risk for a security-relevant file. scripts/security/permission-request-codex.mjs remains implemented and ready to wire in once a build confirmed to support the event is verified. PreToolUse (scripts/security/risk-gate-codex.mjs) holds the actual security boundary; PostToolUse is telemetry-only and is never a security boundary.
